title: Project config file
description: Parameters the tool needs and cannot infer from the record: where the zone sits inside its project, and the window velocity is summed over. The file is .wipctl.toml at the project root, so the root is the directory holding it and nothing is derived. Charter prose states the same cadence for a reader; this file is what a tool reads. No key has a read-time default: a tool finding a required key absent fails its check rather than assuming a value, because a value guessed on a project's behalf is a value nobody wrote down.

plan_dir.description: Path from the project root to this plan zone, relative and without a trailing slash. A project must keep documents somewhere; what that directory is called, how it is organised, and how deep the zone sits inside it are the project's own affair. A common value is docs/plan.

commit.description: Opt-in: present, `wipctl move` commits each transition it performs; absent, it writes the record and commits nothing. Both keys are required whenever the table exists and neither has a default, because a project's commit convention is the project's own.

type.description: The Conventional Commits type the generated message carries.

scope.description: The scope the generated message carries. Lowercase kebab-case, at most two levels.

iteration.description: The window velocity is summed over. Changing either field restarts the series. Presence of this table and its keys is the cross-file checker's fact, not this schema's: the schema owns the types.

start.description: First day of the first iteration, as a calendar date. Without an anchor a tool can only report rolling windows. An instance checker reading TOML presents a native date value here as its ISO string.

length_days.description: Iteration length in days. One cadence per project.

aging.description: Opt-in: present, `wipctl aging` marks rows older than the threshold; absent, bars render with no marks. There is no default threshold.

threshold_days.description: The age in days past which an in-flight entry is marked.

relative_path.description: One or more path segments joined by a single slash. Absolute paths are rejected because they resolve on one machine only; a trailing slash, an empty segment, and a . or .. segment are rejected because a path a tool joins to another must have exactly one spelling.
